prompt: Draw the SAME individual animal as the attached reference image (its accepted side view): same anatomy, same proportions, same colours and markings, same size on the canvas, seen from the view this job asks for. A creature sprite for RimWorld: the siezer. A mud-whale of the Miasma's channels: a short, tapering body driven by four broad flippers, carrying a head fully half its own size. Most of that head is jaw, with ranks of overlapping teeth on a heavy hinge. It hauls itself through the silt half-submerged, a long mud-grey ridge with two small eyes. Visible features: a short tapering body driven by four broad flippers; a head fully half its body size, mostly jaw; a mud-grey ridge of a back. In this view the animal is seen from behind (rear view). The mud-grey ridge of the back runs down the centre and the four broad flippers spread to either side. At the far end, behind and above the shoulders, the massive head shows as a broad domed skull mass, clearly wider than the shoulders, as wide across as the head in the accepted front view and as large against the body as the head in the accepted side view: the head is about as massive as the whole torso, so the animal reads as big-headed even from behind. The jaw and eyes are hidden on the far side of this domed skull. The tail sits at the bottom of the canvas: a narrow, muscular peduncle that widens into a broad two-lobed fluke, one lobe to each side of the centreline, the same broadened terminal paddle seen in the side view. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, soft painted edges in a deeper shade of the local colour, clean dark outline. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.
